steps.title: Your Italian Heritage
steps.subtitle: These four answers determine your eligibility, the route you'll take, and which documents you need.

questions.label: Which Italian-born ancestor connects you?
questions.hint: Decree-Law 36/2025 (in force 2025-03-28) limits new applications to descendants of an Italian-born parent or grandparent.

questions.label: When did your Italian ancestor emigrate from Italy?
questions.hint: Pre-1912 emigration affects whether naturalization broke the chain; post-1948 simplifies the maternal-line analysis.

questions.label: Did your Italian ancestor naturalize as a US citizen?

options.label: Yes — but AFTER the next generation in the line was born
Yes — BEFORE the next generation was born

questions.hint: If naturalization happened before the next generation in the line was born, the citizenship chain is broken.

questions.label: Does your line pass through a female ancestor whose child was born BEFORE January 1, 1948?
questions.hint: If yes, you must file in the Court of Rome (a '1948 case') rather than at a consulate.

steps.title: Documents You Already Have
steps.subtitle: Anything you already hold drops a task. You can revisit and update this list later.

questions.label: Italian ancestor's birth certificate (atto di nascita) from their Comune?
Italian ancestor's marriage certificate (atto di matrimonio) from their Comune?
Ancestor's US naturalization record (or USCIS 'Certificate of Non-Existence')?
Long-form birth/marriage/death certificates for EVERY generation in the chain?
Apostilles on every US document in the chain?
Sworn Italian translations (traduttore giurato) of every US document?

steps.title: Your Plan & Timeline
steps.subtitle: Jure Sanguinis is a multi-year process. We'll back-date due dates from your target.

questions.label: When do you want to hold Italian citizenship?
Have you already booked a Prenot@Mi consulate appointment?
Have you already engaged an Italian lawyer for your case?

taskRules.description: DL 36/2025 (in force 2025-03-28) limits new applications to descendants of an Italian-born parent or grandparent. Great-grandparent paths filed after that date are largely closed except through court action.

taskRules.taskTitle: Consult a lawyer about great-grandparent eligibility post-DL 36/2025
taskRules.description: Your line runs through a great-grandparent (or further). Under the 2025 reform, consulate applications are no longer accepted. A specialist lawyer can advise whether court action or a different path remains open in your case.

taskRules.taskTitle: Verify the citizenship chain was not broken by naturalization
taskRules.description: If your Italian-born ancestor naturalized as a US citizen BEFORE the next generation in the line was born, the chain is broken. Before investing in documents, confirm naturalization timing via USCIS Genealogy.

taskRules.taskTitle: Plan your '1948 case' in the Court of Rome
taskRules.description: Because your line passes through a female ancestor with a child born before 1948-01-01, consulates will reject the administrative application. The court route is filed in Rome, decided in 18–36 months, and has a very high approval rate when the documentary chain is clean.

taskRules.taskTitle: Identify the Italian consulate with jurisdiction over your US residence
taskRules.description: Consulates only accept applications from residents within their jurisdiction. You cannot shop for shorter wait times. Find your consulate based on your state of residence.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order your Italian ancestor's birth certificate (atto di nascita)
taskRules.description: Contact the Comune (town hall) of birth in Italy directly, or via an agent. Request a multilingual extract (estratto plurilingue, Vienna Convention) which does not need translation. Allow 2–6 months.

documentSlot.label: Italian ancestor's birth certificate
documentSlot.description: Estratto plurilingue from the Comune of birth

taskRules.taskTitle: Order your Italian ancestor's marriage certificate (atto di matrimonio)
taskRules.description: From the Comune where the marriage took place. Same multilingual extract format as the birth certificate.

documentSlot.label: Italian ancestor's marriage certificate
documentSlot.description: From the Comune of marriage; multilingual extract

taskRules.description: From USCIS Genealogy. If your ancestor naturalized, you need to prove the date was AFTER the next generation's birth. If they never naturalized, request a Certificate of Non-Existence of Record as proof.

documentSlot.label: Ancestor's US naturalization record
documentSlot.description: USCIS Genealogy record or 'Certificate of Non-Existence'

taskRules.taskTitle: Order vital records for every generation in the chain (long-form)
taskRules.description: Birth, marriage, and death certificates for each generation between you and the Italian-born ancestor. Long-form (not short-form) — the consulate rejects abstracts.

documentSlot.label: US vital records for the chain
documentSlot.description: Long-form birth/marriage/death certs for every generation

taskRules.taskTitle: Apostille every US document in the chain
taskRules.description: Each state's Secretary of State office issues apostilles for state-issued records. Federal records (naturalization, FBI) are apostilled by the US Department of State. $5–$25 per document plus 2–8 weeks per submission.

documentSlot.label: Apostilled US documents
documentSlot.description: Apostille from each issuing state + US DoS for federal records

taskRules.taskTitle: Get sworn Italian translations (traduttore giurato) of every US document
taskRules.description: Translations must be by a translator the Italian consulate recognizes, or sworn in Italy. Each consulate publishes its accepted-translator list online.

documentSlot.label: Sworn Italian translations
documentSlot.description: Traduttore giurato translations of every US document

taskRules.taskTitle: Correct any name or date discrepancies in your documents
taskRules.description: If your great-grandfather appears as Giuseppe on his Italian birth record and Joseph on his US naturalization, you will need a court 'rettifica' or amended US records before submission. This is the most common cause of rejection — review every document line by line.

Italian consulates use the Prenot@Mi system. Citizenship appointments typically have 1–3 year waitlists — book as soon as documents are ordered, not when they arrive. If your consulate's queue is closed, monitor daily.

taskRules.taskTitle: Engage an Italian lawyer for your 1948 case
taskRules.description: Filed at the Court of Rome. Fees typically €3,500–€7,000 for the whole family. Pick a lawyer with a track record of 1948 cases and ask for referrals from prior US clients.

taskRules.taskTitle: Attend your consulate appointment and submit the dossier
taskRules.description: Bring originals and photocopies of every document. The ~€300 fee is paid at the appointment (form of payment varies by consulate). The consulate forwards your dossier to the relevant Italian Comune for registration.

taskRules.taskTitle: File your 1948 case in the Court of Rome
taskRules.description: Your lawyer files the petition with all apostilled + translated documents. You usually do not need to travel to Italy for the hearing.

taskRules.taskTitle: Wait for the Italian Comune to register your birth (trascrizione)
taskRules.description: After consulate approval (or court ruling), your records go to the relevant Comune for trascrizione. This typically takes 6–18 months. Once registered, you are an Italian citizen.

taskRules.taskTitle: Receive your codice fiscale and Italian passport
taskRules.description: Once registered with your Comune, the consulate issues your codice fiscale (Italian tax ID) and you can apply for an Italian passport — a full EU passport granting freedom of movement, residence, and work across the EU.

Anagrafe degli Italiani Residenti all'Estero — the required registry for Italian citizens living abroad. Registration is done through your consulate and is needed to vote and access consular services.

The US taxes citizens on worldwide income regardless of residence. Italy taxes residents (183-day rule). The US-Italy tax treaty covers most overlap. If you intend to retire in southern Italy, also research the 7% flat-tax regime.

taskRules.taskTitle: Register any children's births with the consulate
taskRules.description: Children born to you after you become Italian are automatically Italian, but the birth must be registered (trascrizione) with the consulate to take effect in Italy and the EU.

You need: your birth certificate, your Irish-citizen parent's birth certificate, the Irish-born ancestor's birth certificate, marriage certificates linking the chain, and current government photo ID.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order marriage certificates for every generation where surnames change

taskRules.taskTitle: Search the National Archives of Ireland for ancestor context (optional)
taskRules.description: Free access to the 1901 and 1911 census, marriage licence bond indexes, and other historical records. Useful when GRO has gaps.

taskRules.taskTitle: Gather current photo ID and address verification

Online application via the DFA FBR portal. After submitting electronically, print the form, sign by hand, and post the signed copy with all supporting documents to the address shown on the application.
€270 + €8 postage and handling for adults (€145 + €8 for under 18). Paid online during the application form.

taskRules.taskTitle: Post your signed application and supporting documents
taskRules.description: Use a tracked or registered service. The Department typically returns originals after processing — but allow 12+ months without them.
Currently approximately 12 months. Incomplete applications are delayed further until clarifying documents are received.
Once registered, you are an Irish citizen with the same rights as anyone born in Ireland. The FBR certificate is your official proof.
Once on the FBR you may apply for an Irish passport — a full EU passport granting freedom of movement, residence, and work across the European Union.
Ireland and the US both permit dual citizenship. You retain all US rights; Irish (and EU) rights are added. You can live and work in any EU member state.

taskRules.description: Key inheritance rule: the grandparent path closes if the parent was not on the FBR at the time of the grandchild's birth. To pass Irish citizenship to your descendants, ensure their FBR registration is complete before any of their children are born.

steps.title: Your Restoration Pathway
steps.subtitle: Two free, no-language-test routes exist. The questions below decide which form your application uses.

questions.label: Which historical situation describes your German ancestor?

options.label: Persecuted by the Nazi regime (1933-01-30 to 1945-05-08), lost citizenship
Excluded by pre-1993 paternal-line out-of-wedlock rules
Other discriminatory exclusion (renunciation under duress, etc.)

questions.hint: Article 116(2) Basic Law covers Nazi-era persecution; StAG §15 covers other discriminatory exclusions. Both are free, allow dual citizenship, no language test, no residency required.

questions.label: Which strongest persecution evidence do you have?

options.label: Ancestor named in the 1941 Reichsanzeiger expatriation lists
Yad Vashem testimony / Shoah victims' database entry
Post-war restitution claim under BEG / BRüG
Only ancestor's emigration after 1933 to a country of refuge
Nothing yet — research still to do

questions.label: Do you have minor children to include on the application?
questions.hint: Minors are included on a parent's form; adult children must each file their own application referencing the same ancestor.

steps.title: Documents You Already Have
steps.subtitle: Each box you tick removes a task.

questions.label: German ancestor's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde from a Standesamt)?
Pre-1933 proof of German citizenship (passport, Heimatschein, Meldekarte, military book, German birth registration)?
Documented evidence of persecution between 1933 and 1945?
Long-form birth/marriage/death certificates for every generation in the chain?
Apostilles on every US document?
Certified German translations (ermächtigt / öffentlich bestellt translator) of all non-German documents?

steps.title: Your Plan & Timeline
steps.subtitle: BVA processing currently runs 18–36 months. We back-date from your target.

questions.label: When do you want to hold German citizenship?

taskRules.taskTitle: Confirm your restoration pathway (Article 116 vs StAG §15)
taskRules.description: Article 116(2) Basic Law: for descendants of Germans persecuted 1933-1945 (most commonly German Jews). StAG §15: for descendants of those barred from citizenship by other discriminatory laws (pre-1953 maternal-line, pre-1993 paternal-line out-of-wedlock, etc.). Both are free, no language test, no residency requirement.

taskRules.taskTitle: Identify the persecuted German ancestor and gather initial evidence
taskRules.description: Most commonly: a German Jew stripped of citizenship by the 1941 11th Reich Citizenship Ordinance, or who emigrated and lost citizenship under various Nazi decrees. Searching the Reichsanzeiger 1941 expatriation lists is the gold-standard proof; Yad Vashem and post-war restitution files are also strong.

taskRules.taskTitle: Identify the discriminatory exclusion in your line
taskRules.description: StAG §15 is the catch-all path. Common cases: a child born before 1953-04-01 to a German mother and a non-German father (denied citizenship under prior law); a child born out of wedlock before 1993-07-01 to a German father; renunciation made under duress.

taskRules.taskTitle: Map the documentary chain from you to the German ancestor
taskRules.description: Each generation needs: birth certificate; marriage certificate where surnames change; death certificate where relevant. Note any gaps as acquisition targets. Document any name changes (Schmidt → Smith) that will need affidavit explanation.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order the German ancestor's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde) from the Standesamt
taskRules.description: Each German town has a Standesamt (civil registry). For Jewish ancestors with pre-1875 records, look to synagogue records via Leo Baeck Institute, Yad Vashem, or LDS FamilySearch. Pre-1945 East German records often live at the Bundesarchiv.
Pre-1941 German passport, Heimatschein, residence registration (Meldekarte), military service book, or birth registration in Germany. The consulate publishes a list of acceptable evidence.

Reichsanzeiger expatriation listing is gold-standard. Other strong evidence: post-1933 emigration to a country of refuge, Yad Vashem testimony, naturalization records noting prior German nationality, restitution claims under BEG / BRüG.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order vital records for every generation in the chain
taskRules.description: Long-form birth, marriage, and death certificates between you and the German ancestor.
Germany is a Hague Apostille party. State documents go through the issuing Secretary of State; federal documents (FBI checks, naturalization records) through the US Department of State.

taskRules.taskTitle: Get certified German translations of any non-German documents
taskRules.description: Translations must be by a translator who is ermächtigt / öffentlich bestellt by a German Bundesland. Translations done abroad must themselves be apostilled to be accepted in Germany.

taskRules.taskTitle: Complete the BVA restoration application (StAG-A or StAG-B)
taskRules.description: Article 116 uses BVA-Antrag StAG-A; StAG §15 uses BVA-Antrag StAG-B. Download the current form from the BVA. Minors are included on a parent's form; adults file separately.

taskRules.taskTitle: Submit the application directly to the BVA in Cologne
taskRules.description: Submit by mail to Bundesverwaltungsamt, Postfach 68 06 65, 50728 Köln, Germany. You do NOT need to use a consulate (and skipping it is often faster). No fee.
Current backlog from increased applications. The BVA will request additional documents by mail if needed; respond promptly to avoid restart of the queue position.
Your official proof of German citizenship. Keep multiple certified copies — it's the foundation document for the passport application.

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply for a German passport (Reisepass) at a German consulate
taskRules.description: After receiving your citizenship certificate, schedule a consulate appointment. Fee approximately €82. The German passport is a full EU passport.

taskRules.taskTitle: Understand your dual-citizen status and tax obligations
taskRules.description: Germany has allowed dual citizenship since 2024 (and restoration cases always allowed it). The US taxes citizens on worldwide income; Germany taxes residents. The US-Germany tax treaty handles most overlap — consult a cross-border CPA before relocating.

taskRules.taskTitle: File restoration applications for adult children
taskRules.description: Minor children are included on a parent's application. Adult children must each file their own Article 116 / StAG §15 application referencing the same ancestor — this is much faster than a fresh case since the BVA already holds the ancestor file.

steps.title: Your Polish Heritage
steps.subtitle: Polish citizenship is inherited automatically — these answers reveal whether the chain to you is intact.

questions.label: When did your Polish ancestor naturalize as a US (or other foreign) citizen?

questions.label: Did a male Polish-born ancestor serve in a foreign army between 1920 and 1951 without Polish government permission?
questions.hint: Foreign military service in that window could trigger automatic loss of citizenship. WWII service is treated more leniently in recent case law.

Polish citizenship attorney via power of attorney

questions.label: When do you want to hold Polish citizenship?
Do you have children whose births you'll want transcribed?

taskRules.taskTitle: Confirm a Polish-citizen ancestor with a viable post-1920 connection
taskRules.description: Polish citizenship law took effect 1920-01-31. If your ancestor was a Polish citizen after that date and the chain to you survived, you may already be Polish — the confirmation procedure proves it.

Polish citizenship law took effect 1920-01-31. Ancestors who emigrated from Russian/Austrian/German-partitioned Poland in the 1890s-1910s are usually outside the citizenship-law framework. A specialist lawyer can advise whether any other route applies.

Foreign naturalization before 1951-01-19 broke Polish citizenship under the 1920 Citizenship Act. Before investing in documents, get a specialist opinion on whether any exception applies to your case.
Foreign military service 1920-1951 without Polish government permission could trigger automatic loss. WWII service has lenient case law but is still a flag — get a specialist opinion before filing.

taskRules.taskTitle: Map the documentary chain from you to the Polish ancestor
taskRules.description: Each generation needs: birth certificate; marriage certificate where surnames change. Document name anglicizations (Kowalski → Smith, Stanisław → Stanley) that you will need to explain by affidavit.

taskRules.taskTitle: Find your Polish ancestor's Polish documents
taskRules.description: Polish passport (especially pre-1951), military service book (książeczka wojskowa), Polish parish or civil-registry birth certificate, ship manifest with port of departure, US immigration arrival record, residence registration (zameldowanie).

taskRules.taskTitle: Request the ancestor's US naturalization record (or 'No Record' certificate)
taskRules.description: Via USCIS Genealogy. A naturalization after 1951-01-19 or a 'No Record Found' certificate both preserve the chain.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order birth, marriage, and death certificates for each generation in the chain
taskRules.description: From state/county vital records for US records; from the Urząd Stanu Cywilnego (civil registry) of the relevant Polish gmina for Polish records. Allow 2–6 months per Polish record, longer if parish archives.
Poland is a Hague Apostille party. State documents go through the issuing Secretary of State; federal through the US Department of State.

taskRules.taskTitle: Get sworn Polish translations (tłumacz przysięgły) of every non-Polish document
taskRules.description: Must be by a translator on the Polish Ministry of Justice's official list. Translations done by other translators will be rejected.

taskRules.taskTitle: Engage a Polish citizenship attorney and grant a Polish power of attorney
taskRules.description: Necessary for the lawyer route. Attorney prepares the application, drafts the family-tree diagram (drzewo genealogiczne), and files directly with the voivode by mail.

taskRules.taskTitle: Submit the application (wniosek o potwierdzenie posiadania obywatelstwa polskiego)
taskRules.description: Includes: completed form in Polish, all originals with apostilles and sworn translations, family-tree diagram, power of attorney if applicable, and the filing fee (currently 58 PLN at the voivode, higher at consulates).

taskRules.taskTitle: Wait for the voivode's decision (6–18 months)
taskRules.description: Mazowiecki voivode usually 6–18 months, longer if Polish archive searches are needed. The voivode may request additional evidence by mail — respond within 7 days to avoid delay.
A positive decision confirms you ARE a Polish citizen (and have been since birth, by operation of law). If negative, you can appeal to the Minister of Internal Affairs within 14 days.

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply for a PESEL number (Polish national ID)
taskRules.description: Apply at any urząd gminy in Poland or through your Polish consulate. PESEL is required for passport issuance and most administrative actions in Poland.
Apply at the Polish consulate with jurisdiction over your US residence (or any passport office in Poland). Fee approximately 110 PLN abroad. The Polish passport is a full EU passport.

Poland taxes residents (183-day rule + center-of-vital-interests). The US taxes citizens on worldwide income. The US-Poland tax treaty handles most overlap. Polish PIT is 12% / 32% or 19% flat for business — consult a cross-border CPA before relocating.

taskRules.taskTitle: Transcribe your children's births into the Polish civil registry
taskRules.description: Children born after the voivode's decision are automatically Polish, but their births must be transcribed (transkrypcja) into the Polish civil registry to be recognized for passport applications.

steps.subtitle: Express Entry is points-based. These inputs let you estimate your CRS score on IRCC's calculator and see if you clear recent draw cutoffs.

questions.label: Your age at application
Highest education completed
Your primary-language test level (English IELTS/CELPIP or French TEF/TCF)
questions.hint: Express Entry requires CLB 7+ for FSW (and gives more points up to CLB 10+).

questions.label: Second-language ability
Years of skilled Canadian work experience
Years of skilled foreign work experience
Spouse / partner situation

options.label: Spouse is a Canadian citizen / PR (no spouse-CRS factors)

questions.label: Do you already hold a Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) nomination?
questions.hint: A PNP nomination adds 600 CRS points — effectively a guaranteed Invitation to Apply.

steps.title: Documents & Tests Already Done
steps.subtitle: Tick each item you already have on hand.

questions.label: Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) from WES, ICAS, ICES, or other IRCC-designated body?
Valid language test result (≤ 2 years old)?
Valid passport with ≥ 12 months validity?
Settlement funds proof (~CAD $14,690 single / +CAD $3,955 per family member)?

steps.title: Your Express Entry Plan
steps.subtitle: From profile creation to PR confirmation typically runs 6-18 months end-to-end.

questions.label: When do you want to land as a Canadian PR?
Have you already submitted an Express Entry profile to IRCC?

taskRules.taskTitle: Run your CRS score on IRCC's official calculator
taskRules.description: Use the official Comprehensive Ranking System tool. Compare your score to the cutoffs in the last 6 published draws (general, category-based, French-language, CEC) to gauge your odds of receiving an Invitation to Apply.

taskRules.taskTitle: Take a language test (IELTS / CELPIP / TEF / TCF)
taskRules.description: Required for the Express Entry profile. CLB 7 is the minimum for the Federal Skilled Worker program. Each band above gives more points up to CLB 10+. Book the IRCC-recognized version of your chosen test.

ECA from an IRCC-designated organization (WES, ICAS, ICES, etc.) confirms your foreign education equals a Canadian credential. Allow 6-20 weeks. Not required if your highest degree is from a Canadian institution.

taskRules.taskTitle: Investigate Provincial Nominee Programs (PNPs) in your target province
taskRules.description: A PNP nomination adds 600 CRS points — effectively a guaranteed Invitation to Apply. Each province operates separate streams (tech, health, French-speaking, business) and quotas refresh frequently. Worth pursuing if your unboosted CRS sits below recent cutoffs.

Currently ~CAD $14,690 for a single applicant, plus ~CAD $3,955 per accompanying family member. Bank statements covering 6 months are typical evidence. Not required if you already work in Canada with a valid arranged-employment offer.

taskRules.taskTitle: Renew your passport if it expires within 12 months
taskRules.description: Passport must be valid for at least the full intended PR landing window. IRCC will only issue the Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) on a passport with sufficient remaining validity.

Each NOC-eligible job needs a letter on company letterhead listing job title, start/end dates, hours per week, salary, and detailed duties matching the NOC TEER you're claiming. The duties section is the most common rejection cause.

taskRules.taskTitle: Get a police certificate from every country you've lived in for 6+ months as an adult
taskRules.description: Required by IRCC at the post-ITA application stage but allow 2-4 months for each country. FBI Identity History Summary for the US; equivalent national checks elsewhere. Some certificates are valid for only 6 months — sequence so they're still valid at submission.

taskRules.taskTitle: Create your Express Entry profile in the IRCC portal
taskRules.description: Submit the profile after your ECA and language test are complete. The profile is valid for 12 months. CRS scores are recalculated automatically as your inputs change (additional language tests, work experience, PNP nomination).

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply to a Provincial Nominee Program if pursuing the PNP boost
taskRules.description: PNP application happens in parallel with the Express Entry profile (each province's portal is separate). If selected, the nomination certificate adds 600 CRS points to your EE profile.

taskRules.taskTitle: Wait for Invitation to Apply (ITA) — monitor draw rounds
taskRules.description: Draws happen approximately every 2 weeks. General, French-language, category-based (tech / health / trades / agriculture / transport), and CEC draws each have separate cutoffs. Once invited, you have exactly 60 days to submit the full eAPR.

taskRules.taskTitle: Submit the eAPR (electronic Application for Permanent Residence) within 60 days
taskRules.description: Upload all supporting documents — ECA, language test, work-experience letters, police certificates, medical exam results, proof of funds, family-information form, photos. Application fee currently ~CAD $1,500 (principal + RPRF).
Only IRCC-designated panel physicians can administer the immigration medical. Results are valid for 12 months. Costs vary by country (~CAD $200-400).

taskRules.taskTitle: Receive Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and land in Canada
taskRules.description: COPR is your landing document. Travel to Canada within its validity window (typically 1 year). On entry, present passport + COPR; the border officer activates your PR status.

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply for a Social Insurance Number (SIN) on arrival
taskRules.description: Service Canada offices issue SINs on the spot. You can't be paid legally in Canada without one.
IRCC mails the physical PR card to a Canadian address within ~2 months of landing. You'll need it for international travel as a PR.

taskRules.taskTitle: Enroll in provincial health insurance (3-month wait in most provinces)
taskRules.description: OHIP (ON), MSP (BC), RAMQ (QC), AHCIP (AB), etc. Most provinces have a 3-month waiting period from arrival. Buy private bridge coverage (Manulife / Cigna / similar, ~CAD $80/month) to fill the gap.

taskRules.taskTitle: Understand your dual US/Canadian tax obligations
taskRules.description: The US taxes citizens on worldwide income; Canada taxes residents. The US-Canada tax treaty handles most overlap. File a Canadian return even if you owe nothing — or you lose access to GST/HST credit and Canada Child Benefit.

steps.title: Your Eligibility
steps.subtitle: The UK Ancestry route is open ONLY to Commonwealth citizens with a UK-born grandparent.

questions.label: Which nationality applies to you?

options.label: Commonwealth citizen (Canada, Australia, NZ, South Africa, Jamaica, India, etc.)
British Overseas Citizen / Territories citizen / National (Overseas) / Subject
US citizen only (not eligible — US nationality alone doesn't qualify)

questions.hint: The Ancestry visa requires one of these nationalities — US citizenship alone is NOT sufficient.

questions.label: Where was your UK-born grandparent born?

options.label: Republic of Ireland — born before 31 March 1922
Channel Islands or Isle of Man
On a UK-registered ship or aircraft

questions.label: Are you 17 or older AND able to work in the UK?
questions.hint: Both required. The visa includes a working-intent declaration but no sponsor or skill threshold.

steps.title: Documents You Already Have
steps.subtitle: Each tick removes a task.

questions.label: Your own long-form birth certificate?
Your linking parent's long-form birth certificate?
UK-born grandparent's birth certificate (GRO / ScotlandsPeople / GRONI / Irish GRO)?
Does anyone in your chain have an adoption / legitimation in their record?
Have you spent 6+ months in a country on the UK's TB-screening list?

steps.title: Your Plan
steps.subtitle: Visa decision is ~3 weeks; you must travel within 30 days of issue.

questions.label: When do you want to move to the UK?
Do you already have a UK job offer or freelance contract lined up?
questions.hint: Not required, but strong evidence you'll work in the UK as required by the visa.

questions.label: Do you have bank statements or savings showing you can support yourself without public funds?

taskRules.description: Eligibility is tied to your passport, not your residence. US citizenship alone does NOT qualify. If your only passport is a US passport, the Ancestry route is closed unless you can claim or restore another eligible nationality first.

taskRules.taskTitle: Restore or claim an eligible nationality first
taskRules.description: Your only path forward is to claim another eligible nationality (Commonwealth, British Overseas, Zimbabwean) before applying for the Ancestry visa. If this isn't viable, consider the Skilled Worker or family routes instead.

Birth must be in the UK, the Channel Islands, the Isle of Man, or (before 31 March 1922) what is now the Republic of Ireland. Birth on a UK-registered ship or aircraft also counts. Adoptive and step-grandparents count only if the legal adoption is recognised under UK law.

Ancestry is granted for 5 years. After 5 years of continuous UK residence (with no more than 180 days outside the UK in any rolling 12 months) you can apply for ILR. After 12 more months as a settled person you can apply for British citizenship by naturalisation. Total: ~6 years.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order your own long-form birth certificate
taskRules.description: Long-form (showing both parents' names). The short / wallet-size certificate won't establish the parent-grandparent link.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order your linking parent's birth certificate
taskRules.description: The parent who is the child of your UK-born grandparent. Long-form certificate, not just a summary.

taskRules.taskTitle: Order your UK-born grandparent's birth certificate
taskRules.description: England & Wales: General Register Office (GRO). Scotland: ScotlandsPeople. Northern Ireland: GRONI. Pre-1922 (now Republic of) Ireland: Irish General Register Office.
If you, your parent, or grandparent was adopted or legitimated, include the adoption order or equivalent. UKVI requires evidence the adoption is legally recognised under UK law.

taskRules.taskTitle: Show you can support yourself without public funds
taskRules.description: Bank statements showing sufficient savings, a UK job offer or contract, evidence of freelance income, or a combination. No fixed minimum, but caseworkers expect realistic evidence covering housing + living costs for your first months.

Required if you've spent 6+ months in any UK-listed TB-screening country before applying. Must be at a UKVI-approved clinic. Results are valid for 6 months — sequence so it's still valid at submission.

links.label: Gov.uk — TB test for UK visa

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply online via the UKVI portal
taskRules.description: Application is made online from outside the UK. Current fee is £637 (subject to change) for the 5-year visa. You also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (£1,035/year × 5 = £5,175) as part of the application.

taskRules.taskTitle: Attend your biometrics appointment at a VAC
taskRules.description: Book a biometrics appointment at the VFS Global or TLScontact centre handling UK visas in your country. Provide fingerprints, photo, and submit original documents (or scans, depending on the VAC).

taskRules.taskTitle: Receive your decision and travel within 30 days of visa issue
taskRules.description: Standard processing is ~3 weeks; priority service (~£500 extra) is 5 working days. The 30-day entry vignette in your passport sets the window — you must travel within it and collect your Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) within 10 days of arrival.

To qualify for ILR after 5 years you must not be outside the UK for more than 180 days in any rolling 12-month period. Long absences can reset your settlement clock. Maintain a precise travel spreadsheet from day 1.

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) after 5 years
taskRules.description: After 5 years of continuous UK residence, apply for settlement. Pass the Life in the UK test and meet the B1 English requirement (many Commonwealth applicants are exempt by nationality). Current ILR fee is £3,029.

taskRules.taskTitle: Apply for British citizenship by naturalisation (12 months after ILR)
taskRules.description: After holding ILR for 12 months you can apply for naturalisation. Total time from arrival: ~6 years. Fee is currently £1,500 plus £80 ceremony fee. Dual citizenship with most countries is permitted by the UK.
